A few usual suspects:

1. Every time the parent re-renders, it makes a **new function or object** for that prop — even if it looks the same, React sees a different one and re-renders the child.
2. The child isn't wrapped in `React.memo`, so it re-renders whenever the parent does, no matter what the props are.
3. If you're using context, any change to that context re-renders every component reading it, even ones with unrelated props.

The fix is usually `React.memo` on the child, plus `useCallback` or `useMemo` in the parent so the function or object props stay the same between renders.
